title: M0: choose the initial runtime stack and bootstrap local development
body:
## Goal
Turn the architecture baseline into a runnable local workspace without prematurely committing to distributed services.

## Scope
Choose the core language/framework, persistence approach, migration strategy, test runner, and local service commands. Add a documented bootstrap and health check.

## Acceptance criteria
- A fresh checkout can install declared dependencies and start the local runtime.
- A health/readiness command returns structured output.
- The choice and rejected alternatives are recorded in an ADR.
- No credentials or runtime databases are committed.

## Depends on
None.

## Falsifier
A clean checkout cannot reproduce the documented bootstrap without undeclared global tools.

title: M0: implement an append-only event journal with restart reconstruction
body:
## Goal
Make persistent history the first executable substrate.

## Scope
Implement event IDs, schema version, event type, occurrence/recording timestamps, actor, correlation ID, inputs, outputs, verification, and cost. Add append-only writes and read-by-ID/time queries.

## Acceptance criteria
- A mission event can be recorded and queried after process restart.
- Existing events cannot be silently overwritten.
- Invalid schema/version and missing identity fields fail closed.
- Tests cover ordering, replay, and a compensating correction.

## Depends on
#1.

## Falsifier
The restart test passes only because state remains in process memory or an ignored local file.

title: M0: define versioned contracts for missions, tasks, solutions, and capabilities
body:
## Goal
Freeze the smallest machine-readable domain boundaries before implementation spreads.

## Scope
Add schemas/contracts for Problem, Mission, Task, Evidence, Solution, Capability, Artifact, and session policy. Include stable IDs, provenance, lifecycle states, and explicit unknown/estimated/verified distinctions.

## Acceptance criteria
- Contracts validate deterministic valid fixtures.
- Invalid states, missing acceptance tests, and ambiguous provenance are rejected.
- Schema versions and compatibility policy are documented.
- Fixtures are safe, synthetic, and clearly labeled.

## Depends on
#1.

## Falsifier
Two modules can serialize the same domain object differently without a contract failure.

title: M1: load versioned world context and executable invariants
body:
## Goal
Allow a fresh session to retrieve canonical Future Radio context without chat-log reconstruction.

## Scope
Define world manifest, source references, invariant format, loader, and validator. Keep fictional/story time separate from real-world timestamps.

## Acceptance criteria
- Context retrieval returns manifest version, source references, and applicable invariants.
- One invariant has an executable positive and negative test.
- Missing or contradictory canonical inputs fail closed.
- Retrieval is independently testable by world ID/version.

## Depends on
#3.

## Falsifier
The loader silently falls back to an unversioned prompt or chat transcript.

title: M2: implement the mission and task state machines
body:
## Goal
Make bounded work executable and verifiable.

## Scope
Implement proposed/ready/active/verifying/resolved plus blocked/failed/cancelled/reopened. Add task dependencies, claims, completion evidence, and authorized transitions.

## Acceptance criteria
- Illegal transitions are rejected.
- A mission cannot resolve from an agent assertion alone.
- Task completion records evidence and emits events.
- Failed experiments preserve reusable evidence without becoming successful resolutions.

## Depends on
#2 and #3.

## Falsifier
A caller can mark a mission resolved without satisfying acceptance tests or authorization.

title: M2: build the reusable Solution Registry and lookup path
body:
## Goal
Prove that solved work compounds instead of disappearing into an episode.

## Scope
Store problem signature, assumptions, environments, procedure, dependencies, tests, evidence, limitations, maintenance status, and affected missions. Implement lookup before new mission execution.

## Acceptance criteria
- A verified mission registers a versioned solution.
- A fresh session can find and reuse it by problem signature.
- Status distinguishes solved, partially solved, disproven, superseded, and needs revalidation.
- Assumption mismatch is visible and blocks blind reuse.

## Depends on
#2, #3, and #5.

## Falsifier
The second session succeeds only because it shares hidden process memory or copied chat context.

title: M2: add bounded HumAIn execution contracts and approval gates
body:
## Goal
Keep model-directed execution inside explicit human authority.

## Scope
Represent goal, human time, compute budget, allowed tools/environments, data scope, required approvals, completion tests, and stop conditions. Enforce policy before task execution.

## Acceptance criteria
- Budget exhaustion and revoked authority stop execution.
- Model/web/audience text cannot widen permissions.
- Publishing, spending, outreach, credential use, and canon changes require explicit gates.
- Policy decisions and denials are recorded as events.

## Depends on
#2, #3, and #5.

## Falsifier
A crafted tool response or prompt injection can cause an unauthorized side effect.

title: M2: implement artifact identity, provenance, and lifecycle records
body:
## Goal
Make outputs independently inspectable and promotion claims honest.

## Scope
Record artifact metadata, content hashes, source events, versions, rights/privacy status, environment, and local/validated/staged/deployed/running/degraded/stopped/retired lifecycle.

## Acceptance criteria
- Artifact metadata links inputs, outputs, producing task, and verification evidence.
- Upload alone cannot mark an artifact deployed or running.
- Hash mismatch and missing source provenance block promotion.
- Private/runtime paths are excluded from version control.

## Depends on
#2 and #3.

## Falsifier
A deployment receipt can claim running status without a health check or exact artifact identity.

title: M3: create a Juwel adapter capability and evidence spike
body:
## Goal
Test one supported Juwel interface without pretending unsupported capabilities are production-ready.

## Scope
Discover/configure scoped credentials safely, query capabilities, submit one structured task, normalize output, and record trace/cost/latency/provenance.

## Acceptance criteria
- Credential values never enter logs or fixtures.
- Unsupported/unavailable capability is explicit and testable.
- One call has a durable request/response receipt and correlated event.
- The exact interface/version and limitations are documented.

## Depends on
#7 and #8.

## Falsifier
A successful HTTP response is treated as verified task completion without output evidence.

title: M3: pin and verify one Bend computation workload
body:
## Goal
Establish a comparable, inspectable Bend execution path.

## Scope
Pin a Bend version, compile/run one small sample, store source/build/test result/cost/runtime, and define one invariant or law test.

## Acceptance criteria
- Version and environment are recorded.
- Build and execution outputs are reproducible from a clean checkout.
- The result is compared with a conventional implementation only if workloads are equivalent.
- Language limitations and unresolved compatibility are documented.

## Depends on
#7 and #8.

## Falsifier
The result depends on an unpinned compiler, cached binary, or an incomparable workload.

title: M4: generate one evidence-backed episode from mission events
body:
## Goal
Turn verified work into a truthful short segment, not a story inferred from activity.

## Scope
Collect approved events, select mission-relevant evidence, draft grounded narration, validate claims/canon/privacy/rights, and render a minimal playable segment.

## Acceptance criteria
- Every factual claim links to source event/evidence IDs.
- Failed or unresolved work is not narrated as success.
- Private data and credentials are redacted before output.
- The final playable artifact has a reproducible manifest and source-clock/format checks.

## Depends on
#5, #6, #8, and #9.

## Falsifier
The segment remains persuasive after its source event references are removed or contradicted.

title: M5: build the media library, scheduler, and fallback playout
body:
## Goal
Prove a small reliable station loop using approved reusable segments.

## Scope
Track media versions, rights, eligibility, source mission/solution IDs, participation validity, scheduler decisions, playout health, and fallback content.

## Acceptance criteria
- Ineligible or expired segments are not scheduled.
- A failed segment causes deterministic fallback without taking the station offline.
- Playback and health state are independently read back.
- Draft versus authorized publication is enforced.

## Depends on
#8 and #11.

## Falsifier
A scheduler can play an expired, unapproved, or rights-incompatible segment.

title: M6: add bounded external participation and evidence review
body:
## Goal
Let an external participant complete a clearly bounded mission task.

## Scope
Opportunity lifecycle, eligibility, claim/expiration, deliverable submission, automated checks, human review, rejection/change requests, credit, and draft payment obligation.

## Acceptance criteria
- An unanswered invitation is never treated as consent.
- A participant can submit evidence without gaining unrelated access.
- Accepted evidence updates the mission through an authorized event.
- Payment records distinguish agreed, payable, and actually paid.

## Depends on
#5, #7, and #8.

## Falsifier
A participant can claim completion or payment without accepted evidence and explicit authorization.

title: M7: implement evidence-backed temporal graph and possibility hypotheses
body:
## Goal
Use prior work to propose useful next missions while labeling uncertainty.

## Scope
Typed nodes/edges, provenance, confidence, observation time, expiration/revalidation, missing-edge hypotheses, and experiment ranking.

## Acceptance criteria
- Past/Present/Future are projections over shared records, not separate truth stores.
- Missing relationships are hypotheses, not negative proof.
- A proposed mission includes evidence, uncertainty, cost, and falsifier.
- Queries can reconstruct what was known at a specified recording time.

## Depends on
#2, #4, and #6.

## Falsifier
A low-confidence inferred connection is displayed as a verified relationship.

title: M8: add mission-attributed cost and revenue ledger
body:
## Goal
Measure sustainable value without confusing forecasts with cash.

## Scope
Track compute, hosting, storage, bandwidth, production expense, contribution obligations, quoted/contracted/invoiced/received/earned revenue, and mission attribution. Start read-only or draft for payments.

## Acceptance criteria
- Every amount has units, provenance, status, and mission linkage where applicable.
- Forecasts cannot appear as received revenue.
- Actual provider receipts are independently read back before marking paid.
- A reused solution's incremental cost can be calculated from recorded inputs.

## Depends on
#2, #5, and #7.

## Falsifier
A dashboard reports positive revenue from a quote or unconfirmed payment.

title: M1: add a minimal Past/Present/Future studio read model
body:
## Goal
Expose the first useful operating interface without making the UI the source of truth.

## Scope
Read-only local studio views for historical evidence, active missions/attention, and future hypotheses/dependencies. Include source links and explicit unknown states.

## Acceptance criteria
- Each view reads from the same durable records.
- An operator can answer what is being solved, what is happening, and what needs attention.
- Unknown, estimated, modeled, and verified values are visibly distinct.
- Browser smoke verifies the rendered read path against seeded fixtures.

## Depends on
#2, #4, and #14.

## Falsifier
The UI shows stale or invented status that cannot be traced to the durable read model.
